analysis: The PR changes documentation only: inference.md gets one new failure-mode row (line 2371) about Autopilot placement holds, and model-autopilot.md is substantially expanded. The remaining inference.md text (MiMo, Flint and related sections) is replayed context. It is not in the changed ranges, and I found no new security claims there. The Autopilot doc describes behavior the supplied evidence cannot verify, because the Swift sources are not in the diff. (1) The model set widens from the persisted selection to every verified cached catalog build, capped at 256 IDs. The doc says it never changes the consent revision. (2) Downloads are on by default with consent. The doc lists checks: closed refusal codes, a 50 GiB disk reserve, a catalog active-build and weight-hash check, a ledger, and no advertising, loading or deleting. The one gap I flagged is the absence of default storage and model caps. (3) Adoption and hold placements let a succeeded operation's model be served without a live lease, and hold slots are excluded from eviction. That gives the controller some influence over memory availability, while the doc says cold loads into free memory proceed and holds expire. (4) A transition watchdog cancels only stalled operations. (5) The provider re-registers on an idle tick to publish new inventory. Unverified: whether the implementation enforces the weight-hash and manifest verification and the ledger permissions as described, and whether the coordinator trust assumptions (the coordinator is trusted) cover controller-driven downloads. Integration should check ProviderLoop+AutopilotDownload.swift and AutopilotDownloadLedger.swift against this doc.

findings.detail: The updated doc says that with saved Autopilot consent, a controller can download catalog builds on the operator's behalf unless the operator opts out. Previously, 'downloads' were explicitly not authorized. The documented config table makes `max_storage_gb` and `max_models` default to absent (no cap), leaving only a 50 GiB free-disk reserve as a default guard. A compromised or misbehaving controller or coordinator could use `prefetch_model` to fill the model-cache volume, up to 50 GiB of free space remains. That degrades provider availability (T-016-style disk pressure) and widens the A-004 weights and TB-002 trust surface. Consent is the only gate, and consent was originally for model selection, not bulk downloads. Fix: default to bounded `max_storage_gb` and `max_models`, or require a separate explicit download opt-in. Update the threat model to cover controller-initiated downloads. The implementing code is not in this doc-only diff, so the behavior is unverified.
findings.title: Autopilot downloads become default-on for consented Macs with no default storage or model cap
